prerequisites: Knowledge of all mathematics and physics content taught in the first year of the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and analyze the different components of electrical circuits and master the techniques for their analysis.
Master the analysis techniques for electrical circuits powered by sinusoidal sources.
Identify, analyze and calculate balanced three-phase circuits and their application in industrial electrical installations.
Master the procedures and instruments for measuring electrical circuits.
Describe and analyze the operating principle of electrical machines and their applications.

syllabus_topics: Electric charges, electric current intensity, electric charge, electric voltage between two points and electromotive force, electric power, electric energy. Multiples and submultiples.
Introduction to active and passive elements of electrical circuits
Fundamental topological entities of electrical circuits: branch, node, loop, graph, planar circuit, mesh
Series and parallel connection of elements
Periodic waveforms: period, cycle, frequency, phase shift between waves, peak values, peak-to-peak value, average value, RMS value

Ideal passive elements: resistance (Ohm's Law, resistance (R), conductance, short circuit, open circuit, ideal switch, resistance of a conductor, resistivity and conductivity, instantaneous power dissipated, dissipated energy and Joule effect, real resistances, color code)
Ideal active elements: ideal voltage sources, ideal current sources, series and parallel association of ideal voltage and current sources, ideal dependent sources
Associations and equivalences of ideal passive elements: operational impedance and admittance (generalization of Ohm's Law), series association, parallel association, Kennelly's Theorem
Real active elements: real voltage sources, real current sources, Maximum Power Transfer Theorem, equivalence between real voltage and current sources
Measurement elements: ideal ammeters and voltmeters
II. CIRCUITS IN SINUSOIDAL STEADY STATE
Sinusoidal waveforms: relevance, amplitude, angular frequency, phase angle, initial phase angle, specific characteristic parameters of periodic waves
Complex representation of sinusoidal waves: phasors
Response of R, L, C, RL and RC series dipoles in sinusoidal steady state: phasor diagram
Systematic analysis of circuits in sinusoidal steady state in the complex domain
Power and energy in sinusoidal steady state
Concepts of active, reactive and apparent power
Instantaneous power and energy, and active, reactive and apparent power in R, L, C, RL and RC series dipoles
Power factor: concept, relevance and correction
Circuit resolution using the loop method
Circuit resolution using the node method
Balanced and unbalanced three-phase voltage systems
Line and phase magnitudes, and relationship between them
Active, reactive and apparent power in three-phase elements
Complex power, Boucherot's Theorem, power factor
Power factor correction in three-phase installations
Introduction to the generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy. Short-circuit powers
Introduction to synchronous and asynchronous machines
P1: Description of equipment and assembly of DC circuits
P2: Assembly of circuits in sinusoidal steady state I
P3: Assembly of circuits in sinusoidal steady state II
teaching_methods: Study of theory and problem solving
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is the sum of points from Classroom Practicals (PA, max 1 point), Laboratory Test (PL, max 1 point), and Final Exam (PF, max 8 points). For the extraordinary call, the final grade is the sum of Previous Grade (NP, max 2 points, including PL and PA) and a Final Exam (PF, max 8 points). For differentiated assessment, the final grade is the sum of a Laboratory Exam (PL, max 1 point) and a Final Exam (PF, max 9 points). No minimum score is required for any component to present for the final exam in any assessment type.
